correctness.rationale: For synchronous threshold-one three-state Greenberg–Hastings on the simple-neighbor graph with vertices (row∈Z2,column∈Zn), n>=3, Moore adjacency is all distinct sites at horizontal distance≤1 except self; the two vertical offsets collapse to one opposite-row site. The only third-return nonzero histories must advance 0→1→2→0 everywhere; otherwise the connected cycle constraints yield the all-zero fixed state. Thus each color in each column must have a successor-state neighbor, an exact three-slice local condition, and global labelled period-three states biject with length-n closed walks of a fully specified 81×81 overlapping-column adjacency. Independently constructed the 81x81 binary transfer from the literal update, counted exactly 585 directed edges and factored det(xI-T)=x^74(x^2+3x+9)^2(x^3-6x^2-9x-18). Its Newton/trace identity yields S_n=a_n+4*3^n*cos(2πn/3), a_0=3,a_1=6,a_2=54, a_n=6a_{n-1}+9a_{n-2}+18a_{n-3}; the cubic Perron root ~7.516067898568. Independent ORIGINAL-dynamics enumeration of all 3^(2n) configurations at n=3,4,5 gave 540,3024,23490 third-return states, exactly the transfer counts; transfer counts also independently checked n=6,7,8. Since 7.516...<9, the fraction of immediate period-three globally rotating states tends to zero. Disjoint pairs of columns give at least floor(n/2) independent rainbow triangles with failure (7/9)^floor(n/2), proving a perpetual local three-clock with probability tending one (not globally periodic). Infinite family rests on exact finite matrix identity plus an elementary independent local-obstruction probability bound; finite samples alone do not imply the result.
